subject: Applied Microeconomic Theory
topic: Strategic Form Games, Dominance Solvability, and Pure Nash Equilibrium
syllabus_context: Unit II: Non-Cooperative Game Theory. Strategic (normal) form games, players, action profiles, payoff functions, strictly and weakly dominated strategies, Iterated Elimination of Strictly Dominated Strategies (IESDS), definition of Nash equilibrium in pure strategies, best-response correspondences, Prisoner's Dilemma, coordination games, and Pareto efficiency.
declared_learning_objective: Formulate strategic form games with payoff matrices, solve games via Iterated Elimination of Strictly Dominated Strategies (IESDS), identify pure-strategy Nash equilibria using best-response analysis, explain why dominant-strategy equilibria may be Pareto inefficient (Prisoner's Dilemma), and evaluate conditions where pure equilibria fail to exist or multiple equilibria arise.

provenance.source: Standard Academic Microeconomic Theory Lecture Series

recording_quality.known_observability_limitations: 2x2 and 3x3 strategic payoff matrices written on chalkboard with payoff coordinates (u1, u2).
